Budweiser Clydesdales to lead Christmas on Deer Creek

By JON ALVERSONJON ALVERSON - Publisher
Thu,10/01/26-1:27PM, 1,349 Reads

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:13
Instaread

Christmas on Deer Creek will return to downtown Leland on Dec. 5, featuring a full day of family activities, a 2 p.m. parade, Santa Claus’ arrival by boat about 5 p.m., live entertainment and a fireworks finale, organizer Sherry Smythe said.

Smythe, often called Leland’s “Christmas tree lady,” discussed plans for the annual celebration during a recent community presentation. She said the free event has grown steadily since it began after the COVID-19 pandemic, when she envisioned transforming downtown into a holiday destination reminiscent of a Hallmark Christmas movie.

“Christmas on Deer Creek is our main event,” Smythe said. “We like to shine bright on this event. We want everybody to come from all around and enjoy what we have to offer.”

This year’s celebration will include vendors, a children’s brunch themed around “The Nutcracker,” horse-drawn carriage rides, synthetic ice skating, bumper cars, a rock wall, an electric train from Memphis, visits with Santa Claus and Mrs. Claus, children’s storytelling and a new bucking reindeer ride.

The children’s brunch will offer three seatings, Smythe said. Tickets traditionally sell out online within 10 to 15 minutes, although major sponsors receive tickets and may select their preferred seating time. Chick-fil-A has sponsored the brunch, which includes a children’s meal, a craft activity and character appearances.

The event’s parade will begin at 2 p.m. and will be open to community participants without an entry fee. Smythe encouraged residents, businesses and organizations to decorate vehicles, carts or other entries and participate.

The Budweiser Clydesdales will lead this year’s parade, a new attraction that Smythe described as a major surprise for the festival.

“We have a really big surprise,” she said. “The first thing that you’ll see is the Budweiser Clydesdales coming down the street.”

Santa Claus is expected to arrive on Deer Creek at about 5 p.m. The celebration also will feature the B.B. King All-Stars, along with additional acts before a George Strait tribute performer from Texas takes the stage as the main act.

Fireworks will follow the concert. Smythe said the display, set behind the stage, is a centerpiece of the festival and helps provide the event with a storybook-style ending.

“There’s no admission charge to come,” Smythe said. “It’s really open to everybody, and it’s a family fun day.”

Downtown transformation

Smythe said Christmas on Deer Creek began as an effort to revive downtown Leland and encourage residents and business owners to invest in the area.

When planning began, she said, many downtown buildings had broken windows, deteriorating interiors and few active businesses. Rather than see vacant structures removed for parking, she said organizers focused on attracting businesses and creating a downtown district where visitors could shop, dine and spend time.

“People come and spend money in our town,” Smythe said.

The festival’s growth has coincided with new businesses in downtown Leland, including The Next Chapter bookstore, Renew Collective Studio, West of 55 clothing store, Lagniappe interior design store and Brocante, a business offering food and vintage merchandise.

Smythe’s family also plans to open Clementine, a coffee shop named for her mother-in-law, Margaret Clementine Slyke. The business was expected to hold a soft opening Oct. 15 and will offer breakfast, lunch and coffee.

Smythe said the festival has attracted visitors from throughout the region, including Mississippi communities, Arkansas and organized bus groups from Oxford and Jackson.

Volunteers sought for Nov. 1 decorating

Downtown decorating for Christmas on Deer Creek will begin Nov. 1, Smythe said. Volunteers known as the Red Apron Ladies help install wreaths, lights, bows and other decorations throughout the downtown area.

The group decorates bridges along Deer Creek, and organizers have invested in durable holiday displays intended to be reused for several years. Smythe said additional volunteers are welcome.

Vendor applications also are available for food and marketplace vendors, including artists, crafters and businesses selling children’s items, pottery or other merchandise. Sponsorship opportunities remain available as well.

Smythe said the event has become more than a holiday celebration, serving as a way to introduce visitors to Leland and generate support for downtown businesses.

“It still makes me cry when I see it,” she said. “It is a really exciting thing to see what’s happened in Leland.”
